CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Government is the Central Government. 2. Region is Bantul Regency. 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency. 7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threat of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim. 10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or statements with sexual nuances, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency. 19. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session. 29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner. 30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence. 31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services. 32.

Article 13

1. In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, consisting of fields.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.
4. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.
5. In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (4), then victims of violence shall be referred to other institutions.

Article 24

Ayat (1) Sufficiently clear Ayat (2) Huruf a What is meant by “working network” includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups in the community. What is meant by “coordination” includes: planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs.

Huruf b What is meant by “violence prevention system” includes: mapping locations or areas prone to violence and conducting promotive and preventive efforts to the community.

Huruf c What is meant by “Critical education on the rights of children and women” is an effort to build awareness of children and women about their rights. The purpose of implementing critical education is to help make decisions and not become victims of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for the community consist of: training on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and providing understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Child Protection.

Huruf d Socialization can be carried out through mass media, electronic media, and direct outreach to the community.

Article 3

Ayat (1) Sufficiently clear Ayat (2) Huruf a What is meant by the “prevention” aspect is a protection strategy effort through:

a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, as well as life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes resolving conflicts without violence, skills to handle stress, resource management, making effective decisions, effective interpersonal communication, and guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.

b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self-assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.

c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur; what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling and stress management training.

Huruf b What is meant by the “service and assistance” aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Huruf c What is meant by the “empowerment” aspect is the process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection for women and children broadly.

Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

Article 42

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
a. an employment opportunity information system for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for children and women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for children and women victims of violence who are vulnerable to dropping out of school; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of a joint agreement.

Article 2

The principles of organizing the protection of Children and Women from acts of violence are:
a. respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. the best empowerment for victims.

Article 11

The obligations and responsibilities of society towards the protection of children and Women Victims of violence are:
a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women; b. to provide education on a culture of peace and gender equality; c. to provide information and/or report if acts of violence against children and women occur to law enforcement officials or authorized parties;
d. to protect victims; and e. to provide emergency assistance.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 46

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of violence.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing Child and Women Protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of the rights of Children and Women independently;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

REGIONAL GAZETTE OF BANTUL REGENCY YEAR 2013 NUMBER 15

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 25

Huruf a Prevention efforts in the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members.

Huruf b Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, seeking to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.

Huruf c Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Article 4

Huruf a What is meant by “the right to have their dignity and worth as human beings respected” is upholding human rights.

Huruf b What is meant by “recovery of health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim” is assistance provided by health experts (doctors) for physical disorders suffered and by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim’s mental condition.

Huruf c Sufficiently clear Huruf d What is meant by “obtaining information” is access and information about the whereabouts of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments containing values, meanings, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Huruf e What is meant by “confidentiality of identity” is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Huruf f What is meant by “optimal service” is service that includes medical, medicolegal ektensial, psychosocial and legal.

Huruf g What is meant by “the right to compensation” includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills. Huruf h What is meant by “continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage” is handling that does not stop until physical and psychological healing, legal assistance to restore civil rights, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of good name and citizenship.

Huruf i What is meant by “the right to complaint handling” is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Huruf j Sufficiently clear Huruf k What is meant by “the right to assistance” includes: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members. Meanwhile, legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and during the legal process.

Huruf l Sufficiently clear

Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence. 33. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators in accordance with predetermined standards. 34. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs. 35. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to returning and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims. 36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency. 40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources. 41. Violence Victim Protection Forum hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against Children and Women whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 39

1. In an effort to guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights, the Regional Government cooperates with the Children's Forum that has been established.
2. The Children's Forum is an organization whose members are children who become administrators of children's organizations, studios or groups of children's activities and the like which are generally based on the development of talents, interests, abilities and use of leisure time.
3. The Children's Forum has the following duties:
a. to socialize about acts of violence to peers;
b. to be actively involved in the planning of policies, programs and activities related to the protection of children from acts of violence;
c. to be a source of information on incidents of violence in their environment; and
d. to consult the needs and desires of child victims of violence to partners from related sectors.

Article 34

Legal services as referred to in Article 29 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

The obligations and responsibilities in organizing protection for children and women victims of violence are:
a. Regional Government;
b. society;
c. family; and d. parents.

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 13

1. In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, consisting of fields.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.
4. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.
5. In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (4), then victims of violence shall be referred to other institutions.

Article 3

a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, as well as life skills training for women and children. Article 2

a. respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. the best empowerment for victims.

Article 39

1. In an effort to guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights, the Regional Government cooperates with the Children's Forum that has been established.

a. to socialize about acts of violence to peers;
b. to be actively involved in the planning of policies, programs and activities related to the protection of children from acts of violence;
c. to be a source of information on incidents of violence in their environment; and
d. to consult the needs and desires of child victims of violence to partners from related sectors.

Article 33

Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 29 letter d are services provided by assistants in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide social support so that victims have confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems, by:
a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

Article 40

1. In an effort to provide and organize handling of services and protection for victims, PPT establishes FPKK.

a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of PPT services;

a. health role;
b. psychology role;
c. legal role;
d. social role; and
e. economic role.

Article 42

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.

Psychology services as referred to in Article 29 letter g aim to:
a. provide psychological assistance and services; and

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

d. to protect victims; and e. to provide emergency assistance.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Government is the Central Government. 2. Region is Bantul Regency. 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency. 7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threat of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim. 10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or statements with sexual nuances, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency. 19. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session. 29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner. 30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence. 31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services. 32.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Government is the Central Government. 2. Region is Bantul Regency. 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency. 7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threat of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim. 10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or statements with sexual nuances, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency. 19. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session. 29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner. 30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence. 31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services. 32.

Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

Article 2

The principles of organizing the protection of Children and Women from acts of violence are:
a. respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. the best empowerment for victims.

Article 3

Ayat (1) Sufficiently clear Ayat (2) Huruf a What is meant by the “prevention” aspect is a protection strategy effort through:

a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, as well as life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes resolving conflicts without violence, skills to handle stress, resource management, making effective decisions, effective interpersonal communication, and guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.

b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self-assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.

c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur; what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling and stress management training.

Huruf b What is meant by the “service and assistance” aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Huruf c What is meant by the “empowerment” aspect is the process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection for women and children broadly.

Article 11

The obligations and responsibilities of society towards the protection of children and Women Victims of violence are:
a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women; b. to provide education on a culture of peace and gender equality; c. to provide information and/or report if acts of violence against children and women occur to law enforcement officials or authorized parties;
d. to protect victims; and e. to provide emergency assistance.

Article 42

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
a. an employment opportunity information system for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for children and women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for children and women victims of violence who are vulnerable to dropping out of school; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of a joint agreement.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 46

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of violence.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing Child and Women Protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of the rights of Children and Women independently;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 13

1. In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, consisting of fields.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 2

Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Letter b What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d What is meant by "the best empowerment for victims" is all recovery, rehabilitation, reunification actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the main consideration.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Government is the Central Government. 2. Region is Bantul Regency. 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency. 7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threat of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim. 10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or statements with sexual nuances, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency. 19. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved. 27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session. 29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner. 30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence. 31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services. 32.

RIYANTONO

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 13

1. In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, consisting of fields.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.
4. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.
5. In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (4), then victims of violence shall be referred to other institutions.

Article 2

The principles of organizing the protection of Children and Women from acts of violence are:
a. respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. the best empowerment for victims.

Article 11

The obligations and responsibilities of society towards the protection of children and Women Victims of violence are:
a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women; b. to provide education on a culture of peace and gender equality; c. to provide information and/or report if acts of violence against children and women occur to law enforcement officials or authorized parties;
d. to protect victims; and e. to provide emergency assistance.

Article 42

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
a. an employment opportunity information system for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for children and women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for children and women victims of violence who are vulnerable to dropping out of school; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of a joint agreement.

Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 16. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or statements with sexual nuances, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Ayat (1) Sufficiently clear Ayat (2) Huruf a What is meant by “working network” includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups in the community. What is meant by “coordination” includes: planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs.

The purpose of implementing critical education is to help make decisions and not become victims of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for the community consist of: training on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and providing understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Child Protection.
