Article 3

Ayat (1) Sufficiently clear Ayat (2) Huruf a What is meant by the “prevention” aspect is a protection strategy effort through:

a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, as well as life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes resolving conflicts without violence, skills to handle stress, resource management, making effective decisions, effective interpersonal communication, and guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.

b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self-assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.

c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur; what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling and stress management training.

Huruf b What is meant by the “service and assistance” aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 11

The obligations and responsibilities of society towards the protection of children and Women Victims of violence are:
a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women; b. to provide education on a culture of peace and gender equality; c. to provide information and/or report if acts of violence against children and women occur to law enforcement officials or authorized parties;
d. to protect victims; and e. to provide emergency assistance.

Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 46

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of violence.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing Child and Women Protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of the rights of Children and Women independently;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 27

1. The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units on a networked basis.

Article 2

The principles of organizing the protection of Children and Women from acts of violence are:
a. respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and d. the best empowerment for victims.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 44

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of PPT Minimum Service Standards.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, funding, quality, control and supervision.
5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is the manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will be increasingly better. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 46

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of violence.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing Child and Women Protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of the rights of Children and Women independently;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER I
